content.jointProblem: Can an uncertainty-aware spatial and actuarial model link incompletely located farm policies to hail exposure and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments more reliably than municipality-level loading? The first experiment would audit location accuracy and weather resolution, then test whether transferring the researcher’s spatial-extreme and Bayesian pricing methods to hail improves held-out claim-cost prediction and calibration, without assuming daily five-kilometre data can resolve individual fields.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly relevant experience in Bayesian credibility-based insurance pricing, providing a methodological basis for estimating heterogeneous policy risks from limited claims experience.

sources.quote: classic credibility estimators can be embedded in a Bayesian linear model with conjugate normal–inverse-gamma priors.

rationale.text: His work on spatial dependence in extreme events is relevant to modelling geographically concentrated hail losses, although the demonstrated application concerns water-network pressure rather than hail.

sources.quote: A spatial analysis using a max-stable process model reveals a correlation range of approximately 2.1 km

rationale.text: He contributes probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification to agricultural sensor research in the region, offering relevant experience with imperfect environmental observations.

sources.quote: Struhár leads the work package on probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification, contributing Gaussian process and Bayesian hierarchical methods tailored to irregular and energy-constrained sampling schedules.

rationale.text: His property-insurance consulting experience covers model specification, data pipelines and regulatory documentation, which are relevant to moving beyond exploratory maps into pricing use.

sources.quote: a sensor-based premium adjustment scheme for commercial fire risk, covering model specification, data pipeline requirements, and regulatory documentation.

rationale.text: His project experience includes modular risk-modelling pipelines intended for organisations without dedicated data-science teams.

sources.quote: fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models suitable for small and medium enterprises that lack dedicated data science teams.

constraints.text: Field-level attribution must account for both coarse weather observations and uncertain policy locations; fine-resolution hail estimates cannot be treated as observed ground truth.

sources.quote: daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Initial development and validation must respect the limited claims history and portfolio size; spatially and temporally separated evaluation must avoid treating correlated storm losses as independent evidence.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must support automated pricing integration rather than stop at GIS visualisation, with compatibility assessed against the existing Python batch workflow.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Implementation and maintenance responsibilities must fit the company’s shared operational staffing rather than presume a dedicated research or deployment team.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Data-access planning should accommodate the researcher’s preference for a formal data-sharing agreement before policy and claims records are exchanged.

sources.quote: He prefers collaborations where data-sharing agreements can be established formally; his department has a standard template for this.

risks: The supplied evidence does not establish hail reconstruction or farm geocoding expertise. Transferring methods from pressure extremes, agricultural microclimates and motor pricing requires explicit testing in the first experiment; additional meteorological or geospatial expertise may be needed.

Daily five-kilometre weather data and settlement-only addresses may not contain enough information for defensible field-level exposure estimates. Without finer observations or parcel locations, only coarser risk estimates may be supportable.
Three claim years may contain too few independent hailstorms to validate spatial extremes or stable pricing differences, even if there are many individual claims.
The reported 18% claims excess does not by itself establish exposure mismeasurement as the cause; severity inflation, coverage differences or other portfolio factors could explain some of it.
Researcher availability for a joint project, company budget and delivery timeline are unknown.
Deployment could stall despite a useful prototype: the company’s earlier flood-mapping collaboration was completed but has not been integrated into pricing.
questions: What joint-project time can the researcher commit, and what company budget, delivery timeline and named pricing/IT owners are available?
Can the company supply parcel boundaries or verified coordinates for insured assets, and how do geo-tagged loss locations relate to settlement-only policy addresses?
Which hail variables, timestamps, historical coverage and uncertainty information does MeteoVoj provide, and do its licence terms permit research use and derived pricing outputs?
Are independent radar, hail reports or field observations available to test spatial exposure estimates in the first experiment, and who can provide meteorological and geocoding expertise?
Can all policy-years, including policies without claims, be linked to coverage, insured value, exposure duration, deductibles, claim dates and claim amounts?
Which storm/year holdouts, calibration checks and improvements over municipality-level loading would justify proceeding, and what minimum location accuracy is acceptable?
What data-sharing, privacy, access-control and retention arrangements are required, and what actuarial explainability and regulatory review must precede pricing use?
Who will own integration and maintenance of the scoring pipeline, and can the earlier flood-mapping project clarify barriers that this project must avoid?
